title: American goalkeeper Jonathan Klinsmann suffers broken neck after on-field collision
content:
American goalkeeper Jonathan Klinsmann has suffered a broken neck playing for Italian club Cesena on Saturday.

The United States men’s national team hopeful, who is the son of former U.S. manager and Germany great Jurgen Klinsmann, had to be taken off the field on a stretcher in added time of his team’s 2-0 Serie B defeat at Palermo following a collision with an opposition player.

He was taken to hospital where tests revealed that along with a cut to his head, the 29-year-old had sustained a fracture of his first cervical vertebra.

In a statement Cesena said Klinsmann spent the night under observation at the Ospedali Riuniti Villa Sofia — Cervello in the Sicilian capital

“Tests revealed a fracture of the first cervical vertebra, for which the goalkeeper will undergo further tests and a neurosurgical consultation,” they added.

Writing on Instagram on Monday, Klinsmann confirmed the injury means he will not play again this season.

“During the match I suffered a fracture to my spine which will sideline me for a while,” he wrote. “I want to thank everyone on the ground and at the hospital here in Palermo, the fans of both Cesena and Palermo for the warm wishes and of course my friends and family who have supported me over the last few days.

“Good luck to the boys in our playoff push and I will see you all very soon.”

Klinsmann has become an important part of Cesena’s bid for promotion to Serie A this season, with 35 appearances. They are in eighth place, which would secure a play-off spot.

In November he was an unused substitute for the USMNT in their 2-1 friendly win over Paraguay.

In an interview with The Athletic last August, Klinsmann, who was born in Munich but spent much of his childhood in California, said he would “love to be part of” Mauricio Pochettino’s squad for this summer’s World Cup. He has represented the U.S. up to under-23 level and while he has received call ups to the senior side, he is yet to make his senior international debut.
